title: fix(gateway): preserve history fragments across paged reads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing assistant commentary when a small history page splits the display fragments of one stored transcript row.

## User Impact

Complete source-row groups remain reachable when opening and paging history. Ordinary tail and numeric-offset pages can now return directional history cursors, allowing clients to continue through bounded pages without reopening an anchor.

The requested message count is a soft target, including on the initial tail: a complete source group may exceed it. The existing response byte budget and fetchable oversized-message references still apply. Existing numeric pagination remains available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial-tail count cap could return only the final fragment of an assistant row, while `nextOffset` skipped that entire stored row. Reuse the existing source-group pagination policy for both head and offset admission, removing the separate adjacent-only offset cap and strict head slice. Record consumed message endpoints before display filtering and carry those primitive facts into the existing cursor owner; hidden pages can then make progress without retaining another raw-message array.

Native cursor identity, current sharing checks, retained reset intervals, active-leaf and delta metadata remain governed by their existing owners. Claude CLI paging keeps its injected sequence resolver and source-reset semantics. No schema, config or runtime adapter changes.

## Evidence

- Red: published regression-only `b822d73` on frozen `26e71ce` returned only the final answer instead of two commentary fragments plus the final answer. The real SQLite/production history-handler/serialized-frame test failed at the intended assertion; seven siblings passed (149.10 s wrapper, Node 26.12.1, Darwin arm64). Response/transport callbacks were mocked.
- Green candidate: 15 cases passed, followed by five selected final byte-budget/all-hidden/retained cases passing (13 skipped). Together these cover the current 18-case module, including ordinary tail, offset zero/middle, append then older/reverse traversal, hidden progress, byte caps, authorization, rewrite reset and retained physical history. Wrapper wall times: 103.35 s and 70.44 s.
- Siblings: 39 tests passed across four files covering canonical tail pagination, Claude paging, request budgets/fetchable references and history state (80.37 s wrapper).
- Full staged-source independent review and fresh autoreview: no actionable findings through P2. Formatting, actual native staged-content/freshness guard and unchanged candidate identity passed.
- Linux/Node 24.22.1 Testbox: core production types and all 29 selected consumer test-type graphs passed on captured tree `107f694`. Initial lint found one missing test-sort comparator; that one-line correction subsequently passed targeted type-aware lint and its three affected paging cases (15 skipped, 38.60 s wrapper) on the qualified Darwin/Node 26 owner. The original remote wrapper ended with exit 1, including a cleanup-reconciliation warning; this is not an aggregate-green remote run. Exact-head [CI run 40641579246](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40641579246) completed successfully for `dbc7d15`. The [current ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186536#issuecomment-6461186960) reports no findings, Before merge: None, and no Rank-up moves list.

Production: +65/-47 (net +18); tests: +166/-56 (net +110); docs: +2/-1. The production increase records cursor progress at its producer and reuses existing count policy. This is a pagination foundation for bounded history loading; no deployed Firefox heap reduction, live browser/WebSocket proof or performance measurement is claimed.
